steps.question: How big are icons next to text?
steps.why: Larger icons are easier to see.

steps.pick: neutral.500: the quietest text that still reads, 7.0:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.600: We use the quietest readable gray for hints and captions in dark in order to keep muted text a step below secondary text (neutral.700). The step does this by reading 7.67:1 on surface.default and 6.09:1 on surface.raised, the lightest surface it meets. Raised layers fall under 7:1 by the owner's recorded exception for muted text, the one light mode takes too, as the next gray up is secondary's own step. So people read a hint in a menu as well as on the page, because text keeps the AAA floor (accessibility.definition) and the neutral ramp has no step between muted and secondary (color.definition).

steps.question: What rises above the page?
steps.why: Flat is easier to read at high zoom.

steps.question: How soft are shadows?
steps.why: No shadows; borders do the work.

steps.use: A strong border and a dimmed page
steps.why: The dimmed page makes the dialog obvious.

steps.rule: Fills that float above content. In dark, one step lighter than content, so height reads by tone.
steps.pick: neutral.0, the same as content (surface.default): a menu stands out by its edge alone, not by its fill.
steps.darkPick: neutral.200: We use one step lighter than content for menus, dialogs in dark, in order to show height by tone, 1.26:1 on surface.default. The lighter fill does this by the dark-mode depth rule: the higher a layer sits, the lighter its surface. So people see a menu above the page even where its shadow barely shows, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and the roles answer names the layers that rise (elevation.roles).

steps.pick: shadow.none: We use no shadow for menus and dialogs in order to show their height without a cast shade: the scale gives no layer a step here. The missing shade does this by leaving the layer to its border and the dimmed page behind it. So a dialog stands out at any zoom with no blur to read through, because nothing rises (elevation.roles) and there are no shadows (elevation.values).

steps.rule: The 1px edge of a raised layer. In dark, a solid step lighter than the raised surface, so the edge shows where a shadow cannot.
steps.pick: neutral.200: We use the default line's step for the edge of menus, dialogs and other raised layers, in order to give separation between a layer and what lies under it. The ring does this by a 1px line, 1.45:1 on surface.raised, the layer's only edge, as nothing here casts a shadow. So people see where a menu ends on any page, because raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).
steps.darkPick: neutral.300: We use the step above the raised surface for a 1px ring around raised layers in dark, in order to give separation where a shadow barely shows. The ring does this by a solid, lighter line, 1.8:1 on surface.raised (#595959, no alpha), so its contrast can be checked. So people see a dark menu's edge on any page, because dark ships as standard (theming.values), raised layers keep an edge (elevation.definition) and a decorative line has no contrast floor (accessibility.definition).

steps.pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for cards, menus and dialogs in order to make each card read as a separate object, in a calm tone by brand convention. The largest radius does this by breaking the outline with a curve wider than the 6px controls inside it. So a step card reads as one object that holds its fields, because containers get their own corner (shape.roles, shape.count) and the brand is calm and clear (brand.q1).

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?

steps.why: Items in one group sit 16px apart, not the 12px tight gap: generous space between fields stops mis-taps.

steps.pick: neutral.500: the quietest text that still reads, 7.0:1 on surface.default, above the 7:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.600: We use the quietest readable gray for hints and captions in dark in order to keep muted text a step below secondary text (neutral.700). steps.question: How large is body text?
steps.why: Large text is readable for more people.
Large targets help people with motor needs.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Every state, including loading, gets its own value.
Moderate speed is easy to follow.

steps.use: button/focus-ring at focus.ring.width, with an offset
steps.why: Focus must be seen by everyone.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50: We use a step darker than content for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets: 1.16:1 on surface.default and 1.46:1 on surface.raised. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 8.89:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.why: Clear shapes with a word inside.

steps.rule: The edge of a control people must find.
steps.pick: neutral.500: the edge of a control people must find, 7.0:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.600: We use the muted text's gray for the edge of inputs and other controls in dark in order to keep that edge at its level inside menus and dialogs. The edge does this by reading 7.67:1 on surface.default and 6.09:1 on surface.raised, where neutral.500 gave only 4.17:1 on the raised layer. So people find a field in a dialog as easily as on the page, because controls keep the AAA non-text floor of 3:1 with room to spare (accessibility.definition) and dark ships as standard (theming.values).

steps.pick: radius.6: We use the 6px control corner for boxes that grow in order to keep their role, as objects of one family, by inheritance from the control corner. The same radius does this by giving a text area or a list row the curve of the fields beside it. So people see one family of boxes on a form, because the control corner is slight, not a pill (shape.values), and the brand is clear (brand.q1).

steps.rule: A recessed fill, a step below content.
steps.pick: neutral.100, a step below content (1.17:1 on surface.default), so table headers and wells read as recessed.
steps.darkPick: neutral.50: We use one step darker than content for table headers and wells in dark, in order to show depth by tone, 1.16:1 on surface.default. The darker fill does this by the depth rule turned downward: what sits lower is darker. So a well reads as recessed and never as a raised card, because dark ships as standard (theming.values) and depth reads from tone and lines (elevation.definition).

steps.pick: radius.4: We use a 4px corner for badges and checkboxes in order to give marks a role of their own, apart from the 6px controls. The smallest radius does this by keeping a clear rectangle around a word or a check. So a status never looks like a pill button, because badges get their own corner (shape.roles) and the brand is clear (brand.q1).
